newsitem.title: UK: U.S. Treasuries easier in London ahead of data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries easier in London ahead of data.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were slightly softer in London on Friday with trade muted ahead of key inflation and sales data later.
Analysts said there was scope for a short covering rally after the figures, provided the retail sales data did not surprise on the upside.
"It could be a reasonably good day for Treasuries," said Yamaichi international bond strategist Adam Chester.

"Any signs of retail sales coming in relatively subdued, suggesting the U.S. consumer sector may be slowing into the second quarter, could see a reasonably sharp short covering rally in the Treasury market."

By 1005 GMT, the long bond was at 94-00, down from 94-01 in Tokyo and uchanged from the New York close. The June T-bond future was up 1/32 at 107-12 and September Eurodollars were down 0.005 at 93.725.
Chester said with sentiment in the Treasury market so fragile, investors would likely sell into any rally on Friday.
One trader at a European bank here was more pessimistic, saying the market would struggle to push higher going into the weekend.
"It's difficult to see what's going to turn the market up," he said. "The resistance level at 107-26 (for the June future) is proving quite difficult to crack."
But he added that if the market did manage to break that level with any conviction there could be a correction to 109-25.

According to a Reuters survey, economists expect U.S. producer prices to be unchanged in March versus a 0.4 percent fall in February. Core PPI is seen up 0.1 percent on the month, up from a previous 0.1 percent fall.
Retail sales are seen up 0.6 percent in March, versus a 0.8 percent rise in February.
Chester said he would be in the long end of the curve going into the figures.
"On a very short term trade I'd want to be at the long end to get maximum value from any rally," he said, adding he expected continued flattening of the curve medium term.
